introduction: The Báb's book, the Bayán, pointed beyond itself to "Him Whom God shall make manifest." When Bahá’u’lláh made that claim, most of the Báb's followers accepted it and some did not. These passages are addressed to them. They ask the people of the Bayán to be fair, to bring the proof by which they first believed, not to let the letters of the Bayán or attachment to names veil them from the one it promised, and not to repeat what earlier communities did to their awaited ones. A hundred outside voices stand beside them: John the Baptist and those who questioned Jesus, Moses on the prophet to come, Paul on the veil over the old scripture, the Qur’an on peoples who disbelieved in what they had awaited, and Dostoevsky's Grand Inquisitor; with Jude, Paul and the Revelation of John for the duty to guard what has been received.
questions: "By what proof did ye believe in the Primal Point? Bring it forth." How does that test work, and how does it compare with the one in Deuteronomy?
The passages warn that a book can become a veil over the one it promised. Jesus said the same of those who searched the scriptures. How can a scripture be loved without that happening?
Paul forbids "any other gospel," Jude speaks of a faith "once delivered," the Qur’an of a seal. Every community has such words. What is each for, and what do these summonses ask to be done with them?
Bahá’u’lláh tells the people of the Bayán that they are repeating what earlier peoples did. What makes that pattern so hard to see from inside?
Dostoevsky's Inquisitor tells the returned Christ that he is in the way. Why might a faith's guardians resist its fulfilment?
"Cast the names behind you." What names does your own tradition, or your own thinking, hold on to in place of what they point to?

outside.why: John the Baptist said of the one he announced: he must increase, but I must decrease.
John told the crowds that one stood among them whom they did not know, whose shoe he was not worthy to unloose.
Deuteronomy raises the question these summonses press: how shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken? What test does "by what proof did ye believe?" propose?
Jesus says of his hearers that seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not.
This is the verse of the Qur’an that the passage quotes, on the signs people pass by with faces turned away.
The Qur’an tells of a covenant taken from the prophets: when a messenger comes confirming what you have, you shall believe in him and help him.
Moses told his people that a prophet would be raised up after him, and that they must listen to him.
Jesus said to those who studied the scriptures: they testify of me, and ye will not come to me.
The Revelation of John ends by warning anyone who adds to the words of the book. How can faithfulness to a book become what keeps a reader from the one it promised?
John's Gospel says: he was in the world, and the world knew him not; he came unto his own, and his own received him not.
Isaiah hears God invite his people: come now, and let us reason together.
Jesus asks his critics to judge not by appearance, but to judge righteous judgment.
The Qur’an promises signs on the horizons and within themselves until the truth is plain.
Gamaliel warned a council not to oppose a new teaching, lest they be found fighting against God.
Jesus warns of those who come in sheep's clothing and inwardly are ravening wolves.
Ezekiel is told that people come and hear his words as they would a pleasant song, and do not do them.
This is the proverb the passage echoes: the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
Paul's rule is: prove all things; hold fast that which is good.
Paul calls the law a schoolmaster to bring its people to the one who came after it.
Paul says that a veil lies on the heart when the old scripture is read, and is taken away in turning to the Lord.

Dostoevsky's Grand Inquisitor says to the returned Christ: thou hast handed the work on to us; why hast thou come to hinder us? Why might the keepers of a faith be the last to welcome its promised one?
The first letter of John says: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God.
Jesus said: had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me, for he wrote of me.
The Qur’an has Jesus announce a messenger who is to come after him.
Paul says of his own people that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
The Qur’an quotes those who said: we will not believe until we are given what God's messengers were given.
Jesus refuses a sign to those who set conditions, and gives them only the sign of Jonah.
The Qur’an says of God: he will not be questioned as to what he does.
Isaiah asks whether the clay shall say to the potter: what makest thou?
Paul told his converts to accept no other gospel, though an angel from heaven should preach it. How is a believer to be fair to a new Book while keeping faith with the old?
The Qur’an says of the idols: they are but names which ye have named, ye and your fathers.
Exodus tells how quickly a people turned to a calf and said: these be thy gods.
Juliet asks what is in a name, since a rose by any other would smell as sweet.
The Tao Te Ching says that the name that can be named is not the enduring name.
This is the verse the passage hears in the waves: the truth has come and falsehood has vanished.
The Qur’an likens those who were given a scripture and did not apply it to an ass carrying books.
The Qur’an calls Muḥammad the seal of the prophets, and many took that to close the door. What does every community do with the finality of its own book?
Jesus says that new wine must be put into new bottles, or both are lost.
The letter of Jude asks believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. When is that loyalty, and when is it the veil described here?
Paul says that these things happened as examples: let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.
In the parable Abraham says: if they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded.
Moses tells his people that they were chosen for no merit of theirs.
Jesus tells his disciples to proclaim on the housetops what they have heard.
Moses turned aside to see a fire in the wilderness that burned and did not consume.
Daniel saw one like the Son of man come with the clouds of heaven, and dominion was given him.
A psalm asks why the nations rage against the Lord and his anointed.
Malachi hears a promise that the windows of heaven will be opened.
Malachi foretells a messenger who prepares the way, and then the Lord coming suddenly to his temple.
John the Baptist himself sent from prison to ask: art thou he that should come, or do we look for another? Is honest doubt in a forerunner's followers something these summonses allow for?
Peter's confession was answered: flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee.
Isaiah hears: my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways.
Isaiah cries: arise, shine, for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
The Qur’an speaks of a day when thy Lord shall come, with angels rank on rank.
Zechariah foretells a king who comes lowly, riding upon an ass. What kind of sovereignty is claimed by one who writes from exile and prison?
Isaiah says that the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.
John the Baptist said that the one coming after him was mightier than he.
John's Gospel says that the light shines in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.
Jesus wept over a city that did not know the time of its visitation.
Jesus compares his generation to children who will be pleased neither by piping nor by mourning.
Jesus was asked to say plainly who he was, and answered: I told you, and ye believed not.
Stephen asks his judges: which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted?
Jesus says of those who claim they would not have killed the prophets that they are the children of those who did.
The Qur’an says of an earlier people that when what they had been waiting for came to them, they disbelieved in it.
Paul says that those who condemned Jesus fulfilled the prophets that were read to them every sabbath.
Jesus warns that the kingdom will be taken from those who do not bear its fruits.
Paul warns the newly grafted branches not to boast, but to fear, since the natural branches were not spared.
Jesus says to those sure of their sight: now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth.
The Preacher says that what has been is what shall be. Is each people bound to repeat the refusal of the one before, and what would break the pattern?
Paul rebukes a church divided into parties, each calling itself by a different name.
A psalm says of idols that they have eyes and see not, and that those who make them become like them.
In the parable the tenants say of the owner's son: this is the heir; come, let us kill him.
Joseph's brothers cast him into a pit, and said they would see what became of his dreams.
The neighbours of Jesus said: is not this the carpenter's son? and they were offended in him.
Haggai asks: is it time for you to dwell in your panelled houses, while this house lies waste?
Jesus says that the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head.
The Qur’an says that they would put out the light of God with their mouths, and that God will perfect his light.
Isaiah's servant is oppressed and afflicted, and yet he opens not his mouth.
Jesus says that the one who has his commandments and keeps them is the one who loves him.
This is the verse of the Qur’an that the passage echoes: do people think they will be left alone on saying, "We believe," and not be tested?
The letter to the Hebrews recalls Esau, who afterwards found no place of repentance, though he sought it with tears.
Jesus warned his followers to believe no one who said, "Lo, here is Christ." That warning made later claims hard to hear. How is a warning against pretenders to be kept from shutting out the true?
The letter to the Hebrews speaks of those who were once enlightened and fall away.
Paul warns against being children, tossed about with every wind of doctrine by the sleight of men.
Paul tells the Romans to mark those who cause divisions, and avoid them.
The second letter of John says not to receive one who does not bring the teaching.
Paul says that the Creator is clearly seen from the things that are made, so that none has excuse.
Elijah asks the people how long they will waver between two opinions.
The letter to the Hebrews says that God, who spoke in past times by the prophets, has spoken again.
A psalm says that unless the Lord builds the house, they labour in vain who build it.
Jesus says: I have not spoken of myself; the Father who sent me gave me what I should say.
John the Baptist told those who relied on their descent that God could raise up children to Abraham from the stones.
The letter of James calls blessed the one who endures trial, for he shall receive the crown of life.
Jesus says to his disciples, before he leaves them: let not your heart be troubled.
This is the verse of the Qur’an that the passage echoes: in God let believers put their trust.
Proverbs says: trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding.
A psalm says: commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him.
Jesus told his disciples that it was expedient for them that he go away.
Isaiah hears: fear thou not, for I am with thee; be not dismayed, for I am thy God.
Paul says that he counts all things but loss for the sake of the one he has come to know.
Genesis says that the voice of Abel's blood cried from the ground.

matthew-art-thou-he-that-should-come.text: Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another

deuteronomy-prophet-like-unto-me.text: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him. And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him

john-tell-us-plainly.text: Then came the Jews round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou make us to doubt? If thou be the Christ, tell us plainly. Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believed not: the works that I do in my Father's name, they bear witness of me. But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you

matthew-this-is-the-heir.text: But last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son. But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance. And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him

haggai-cieled-houses.text: Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste

hebrews-no-place-of-repentance.text: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears

quran-names-which-ye-have-named.text: They are but names which ye have named, ye and your fathers, for which Allah hath revealed no warrant. They follow but a guess and that which (they) themselves desire. And now the guidance from their Lord hath come unto them.

quran-let-believers-put-their-trust.text: Their messengers said unto them: We are but mortals like you, but Allah giveth grace unto whom He will of His slaves. It is not ours to bring you a warrant unless by the permission of Allah. In Allah let believers put their trust!

quran-till-we-are-given-the-like.text: And when a token cometh unto them, they say: We will not believe till we are given that which Allah's messengers are given. Allah knoweth best with whom to place His message. Humiliation from Allah and heavy punishment will smite the guilty for their scheming.

shakespeare-whats-in-a-name.text: What's in a name? that which we call a rose / By any other name would smell as sweet
shakespeare-whats-in-a-name.author: William Shakespeare

source.label: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (MIT)

dostoevsky-why-art-thou-come-to-hinder-u.text: Thou hast given to us the right to bind and to unbind, and now, of course, Thou canst not think of taking it away. Why, then, hast Thou come to hinder us
dostoevsky-why-art-thou-come-to-hinder-u.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
